name.purpose: "Kacper Rękawek" on the first stage, two lines, about 11vw on desktop and 18vw below 600px. Nothing else reaches this size.

display.purpose: Chapter headlines, sheet heads, the subpage H1 (max 16ch). One line-mask reveal per chapter headline.

headline.purpose: Section heads inside sheets (prices, clauses, process, FAQ, FastBot, the enquiry form) and client names on the work page.

title.purpose: H3s, beat titles in a chapter, the benchmark sentence, prose H2s.

numeral.purpose: Process step numbers in Copper Ink (Lit Copper on the graphite sheet); 3.4rem from 960px.

lead.purpose: The line under a headline; the subpage lead holds 44ch.

body.purpose: Running text at 62ch (prose pages 68ch), lining numerals.

small.purpose: Row notes, breadcrumbs, form errors, beat descriptions.

source.purpose: The source and date under every number, form hints and notices, max 70ch.

button.purpose: Labels on copper and ghost keys.

key.purpose: Labels on header keys; choice and city chips use the same size at weight 400.

label.purpose: Martian Mono, uppercase, width 87.5%: rail keys, footer column heads, field labels and legends (0.02em), row metadata, dates. Never a sentence, never a kicker.

shadows.name: cap-skirt
shadows.purpose: --cap-skirt. The bottom edge of every copper key and the current rail key.

shadows.name: cap-top-light
shadows.purpose: The lit top edge of a copper key, paired with the skirt.

shadows.name: cap-pressed
shadows.purpose: A copper key going down, with translateY(2px).

shadows.name: dark-key
shadows.purpose: Header keys and the phone rail letter keys at rest.

shadows.name: dark-key-hover
shadows.purpose: A dark key under the pointer: the rim brightens, the key does not lift.

shadows.name: dark-key-pressed
shadows.purpose: A dark key going down, with translateY(2px).

shadows.name: ghost-key
shadows.purpose: The hairline key; on hover rim and skirt take currentColor.

shadows.name: rail-tray
shadows.purpose: The studio tray that holds the chapter rail keys.

shadows.name: field-focus
shadows.purpose: Inputs and textareas in focus, with the border turned ink. Not elevation.

shadows.name: frame-drop
shadows.purpose: Screenshot frames laid on a sheet.

shadows.name: frame-drop-hover
shadows.purpose: A screenshot frame under the pointer.

shadows.name: case-frame-drop
shadows.purpose: The large case screenshot on the work page.

shadows.name: chat-drop
shadows.purpose: The cream FastBot chat card on the graphite sheet.

shadows.name: sheet-shade
shadows.purpose: 5rem tall, outside a sheet edge that meets the film: the shade the paper casts on the lit set. A gradient, not a box-shadow.

shadows.name: stage-shade
shadows.purpose: From 960px, behind chapter and opener copy (mirrored for right-side copy); below 960px an opaque studio block under the copy instead.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: --ease. Every state transition, the film and still crossfade, the header band swap, the rail, the menu, value swaps.

motion.name: key-press
motion.purpose: Transform and skirt of a key going down 2px.

motion.name: hover-colour
motion.purpose: Key face and link underline colour changes (inputs and chips 0.15s).

motion.name: header-band
motion.purpose: The dark band behind the header keys swaps for the paper band when a sheet is under it.

motion.name: rail-hide
motion.purpose: The chapter rail slides down 150% (opacity 0.3s) while a sheet or the footer passes under it.

motion.name: film-fade
motion.purpose: The live film fades in over the still of its pose.

motion.name: value-swap
motion.purpose: A swapped readout word rises 0.35em from transparent; counts roll to their new value.

motion.name: headline-reveal
motion.purpose: One line-mask reveal (clip-path from the bottom, 0.4em rise) per chapter headline after the first, on the chapter track own scroll timeline; off under reduced motion.

motion.name: caret
motion.purpose: The Lit Copper caret of the typed greeting blinks while the film runs; it stops when the greeting is sent.

motion.name: chat-playback
motion.purpose: FastBot lines still to come wait at 40% opacity and fade up in turn.

narrative.overview:
kacper.biz is shot like a product: a warm studio-black set with one real object in it, a machined 96% keyboard of exactly 100 keys, three of them solid copper (Esc, K, Enter). Scrolling moves the camera and the board changes pose chapter by chapter; between chapters, flat cream evidence sheets slide over the film and carry the facts. The page's own controls are keys from the same board: the same corner, a darker skirt edge, 2px of travel under the finger.

Density is low on the film and high on the sheets. A film chapter holds one statement: the name or a headline in Funnel Display, a line of Funnel Sans, at most one key. The sheets carry the evidence in rows with hairlines, tabular figures, source lines and forms. Martian Mono appears only where the board itself would print: short labels, counts, dates, the chapter rail and the legends on the caps.

Motion is machined, weighted and damped. The object moves between chapters, the type holds still, and each chapter headline gets one line-mask reveal. Without a GPU, WebGL or JavaScript every stage shows a pre-rendered still of the same pose, and the page stays complete. Refused in the direction: an abstract sculpture, a floating blob, particles, a glowing globe; loud palettes (yellow, red, black) and printed or paper-textured looks.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds only: studio black for the film and its chrome, cream paper for the evidence sheets.
One hue: copper, in three tempers (key face, lit on dark, ink on paper).
Every control is a keycap: 0.6rem corner, 3px skirt, 2px press travel.
One object, one canvas: a fixed WebGL film behind the page, stills in its place when it cannot run.
A monumental name in Funnel Display; Funnel Sans for reading; Martian Mono for data only.
Flat, opaque sheets with hairline rows; depth belongs to the film and the keys.

rules.name: The One Metal Rule
rules.body: Copper is the only hue on the page. It marks the one primary key per screen, the chapter you are in, and the counts that matter. There is no second accent, no gradient on type and no glow in the page UI (in the film, the only emitted light is a pressed legend lighting copper); Error Rust appears only on a failed field.

rules.name: The Three Tempers Rule
rules.body: Copper changes temper with its ground: Copper (#C8703F) is a key face carrying ink; on studio or graphite, copper type is Lit Copper; on paper, it is Copper Ink. Copper #C8703F is never text on paper (2.92:1).

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Everything sits on studio black or on cream paper. A sheet swaps the text variables (text becomes ink, dim becomes worn ink, the dark hairline becomes the paper hairline) instead of inventing new colours; hairlines are always the ground's text colour at low alpha.

rules.name: The Monument Rule
rules.body: The name is set once, largest, in two lines, and runs past the copy column under the object's shoulder. Headlines never borrow its size.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: Martian Mono sets short labels, counts, dates, the rail and the cap legends, always uppercase at label size on the page. It never sets a sentence and never sits above a heading as a kicker.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Figures are lining everywhere; in rows, counts and prices they are tabular, and every market or results number carries a source line directly under it.

rules.name: The Opaque Floor Rule
rules.body: Copy never fights lit metal. On desktop a studio shade (90% to transparent, from the copy side) sits behind the stage copy; on phones an opaque studio block rises from just above the first line, so any part of the object that passes behind text is hidden, never a see-through ghost.

rules.name: The One Object Rule
rules.body: There is one canvas and one object. Subpages hold a single pose of the same board; no second 3D element, illustration or decorative image enters the film side.

rules.name: The Key Depth Rule
rules.body: A control shows depth only the way a keycap does: skirt, top light, 2px travel. No floating drop shadows, no glows, no lift on hover.

rules.name: The Paper Over Light Rule
rules.body: Sheets are opaque and flat. The film sleeps while a sheet covers the screen; the only depth a sheet shows is the shade it casts on the film.

rules.name: The Cap Radius Rule
rules.body: 0.6rem is the corner of a key. A new control uses it; a container around controls adds its own padding to it; a control inside a container subtracts. Never a pill (999px), never a sharp corner on anything the finger presses.

dos: Do make every new control a keycap: the 0.6rem corner, an inset 3px skirt, 2px of travel on press.
Do give each screen one copper key for its single primary action; the second action is a ghost key.
Do put facts on cream sheets laid over the film, in the rows pattern with tabular figures and a source line under every number.
Do use Lit Copper for copper type on dark and Copper Ink for copper type on paper.
Do keep chapter copy on one half of the grid and leave the other half to the object; on phones keep the object in the top half and the copy on an opaque studio floor.
Do keep the page complete without the film: a still for every pose, shorter tracks when the film is off, collapsed tracks and no reveals under reduced motion.

Do let the object move and the type hold still: one line-mask reveal per chapter headline; beyond that only live values move (the greeting typed in step with the keys, a readout count rolling, a swapped word rising 0.35em).
donts: Don't introduce a second hue, a gradient on type, or a glow or bloom in the page UI; copper is the only colour on the page, and in the film only a pressed legend emits light.
Don't add a second 3D object or any abstract form (sculpture, blob, particles, globe); the keyboard is the one object.
Don't set Copper (#C8703F) as text on paper (2.92:1); use Copper Ink.
Don't put a mono label above a heading as a kicker, and don't set sentences in Martian Mono.
Don't give controls pill or square corners, floating drop shadows or hover lifts.
Don't add print texture to the sheets (halftone, registration, grain, leader dots); they are flat cream stock, and grain belongs only to the film.
Don't park the object behind a block of copy on a phone or let copy sit on see-through metal.
